# ML Market Prediction Study -- Results Summary

*Generated by the study pipeline on real data; all numbers below are actual outputs.*

- Sample: `SPY` 2010-02-04 -> 2026-10-06 (4193 usable rows)
- Design: 8-fold expanding walk-forward, test 63d/fold, embargo 1d; holdout = chronologically last 20% of rows
- Transaction cost: 10 bps per position switch

## Headline verdict

No model beats the majority baseline on the holdout: no model shows a significant Holm-adjusted McNemar *improvement* and the best holdout ROC-AUC is 0.5022 -- statistically indistinguishable from chance. gradient_boosting made significantly *fewer* correct calls than the baseline (Holm-adjusted p < 0.05), i.e. it was significantly worse. Under this leakage-free walk-forward design, the study finds **little to no statistically significant incremental out-of-sample signal** beyond simple baselines -- the honest and expected outcome under near-form market efficiency.

Best non-baseline model on holdout: **random_forest** (ROC-AUC 0.5022, accuracy 0.5459; majority baseline accuracy 0.5638). Buy-and-hold over the holdout returned 92.71%; the random_forest long/flat strategy net of 10 bps returned 59.47%.

## McNemar tests vs majority baseline (holdout)

| model               |   model_right_only |   baseline_right_only |   p_value |   p_value_holm |
|:--------------------|-------------------:|----------------------:|----------:|---------------:|
| logistic_regression |                  6 |                    11 |    0.3323 |         0.6516 |
| random_forest       |                 94 |                   109 |    0.3258 |         0.6516 |
| gradient_boosting   |                151 |                   210 |    0.0022 |         0.0111 |
| xgboost             |                141 |                   186 |    0.0148 |         0.0594 |
| mlp                 |                119 |                   158 |    0.0222 |         0.0667 |

*Holm (1979) step-down adjustment across the five non-baseline models; the family is small but the search over models x hyperparameters x metrics is wider -- interpret with Bonferroni-style caution.*

## Best hyperparameters (searched inside walk-forward CV only)

- `majority_baseline`: `{}` (mean fold balanced accuracy 0.5000)
- `logistic_regression`: `{"clf__C": 0.01}` (mean fold balanced accuracy 0.5000)
- `random_forest`: `{"max_depth": 8}` (mean fold balanced accuracy 0.5075)
- `gradient_boosting`: `{"learning_rate": 0.1, "max_depth": 3}` (mean fold balanced accuracy 0.4958)
- `xgboost`: `{"learning_rate": 0.1, "max_depth": 3}` (mean fold balanced accuracy 0.4982)
- `mlp`: `{"clf__alpha": 0.01}` (mean fold balanced accuracy 0.5049)

## Caveats

- No intraday fills; decisions at the close, applied to the next day's return; slippage ignored.
- Single asset (SPY as S&P 500 proxy), single period, one random seed.
- Hyperparameters were selected on the same walk-forward predictions reported as CV metrics -> CV numbers are mildly optimistic (selection/overfitting-the-CV bias); the holdout is the honest estimate.
- This is a study, not investment advice.
